stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite syntomic morphism of schemes. There is a canonical trace morphism of absolute algebraic de Rham complexes
$$\Theta_{Y/X}:f_*\Omega^\bullet_{Y/\mathbf Z}\longrightarrow\Omega^\bullet_{X/\mathbf Z}$$
whose component in degree $0$ is the usual algebra trace $\operatorname{Tr}_f:f_*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$, and which satisfies the projection formula
$$\Theta_{Y/X}(f^*\omega\wedge\eta)=\omega\wedge\Theta_{Y/X}(\eta)$$
for local forms $\omega$ on $X$ and $\eta$ on $Y$. If $f$ is a morphism over a scheme $S$, this descends to a morphism of relative de Rham complexes
$$f_*\Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}\longrightarrow\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}.$$
hypotheses: $f:Y\to X$ is finite syntomic (and, for the final assertion, is over $S$).
conclusions: The finite-syntomic de Rham trace exists, extends the algebra trace, satisfies the projection formula, and descends to relative de Rham complexes over any common base $S$.

source_identity.original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Garel-map-frobenius-smooth-char-p}
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $X \to S$ be a smooth morphism
of relative dimension $d$ of schemes in characteristic $p$.
The relative Frobenius $F_{X/S} : X \to X^{(p)}$ of $X/S$
(Varieties, Definition \ref{varieties-definition-relative-frobenius})
is finite syntomic and the corresponding map
$$
\Theta_{X/X^{(p)}} :
F_{X/S, *}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to \Omega^\bullet_{X^{(p)}/S}
$$
is zero in all degrees except in degree $d$ where it defines a
surjection.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $S$ a scheme of characteristic $p$, and $X\to S$ a smooth morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Let $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$ and let $F_{X/S}:X\to X^{(p)}$ denote relative Frobenius. Then $F_{X/S}$ is finite syntomic. Let
$$\Theta_{X/X^{(p)}}:F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}\longrightarrow\Omega^\bullet_{X^{(p)}/S}$$
be its relative de Rham trace map. All graded components of this map vanish except in degree $d$; in degree $d$ the map $F_{X/S,*}\Omega^d_{X/S}\to\Omega^d_{X^{(p)}/S}$ is surjective.
hypotheses: $X/S$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ in characteristic $p$, with the indicated relative Frobenius.
conclusions: The relative Frobenius is finite syntomic and its relative de Rham trace is supported in top differential degree, where it is surjective.
